tasks.prompt: BMBL CEO CHANGE: Whitney Wolfe Herd RETURNED as CEO in mid-March 2025 after Lidiane Jones resigned 'for personal reasons' in January 2025. Whitney was previously CEO from founding until Jan 2024 when she stepped down. Questions: 1) Why did Lidiane Jones resign after only ~1 year? 2) Is Whitney's return a sign of strength (founder returns to save company) or desperation (nobody else wants the job)? 3) Compare to other founder returns: Steve Jobs at Apple, Howard Schultz at Starbucks, Jack Dorsey at Twitter. 4) What has Whitney changed since returning? 5) She exercised options and sold $6.3M at $6.26 in Aug 2025 — is this a red flag?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a corporate governance analyst. Founder returns are either the ultimate bull signal (Jobs/Apple) or a sign of chaos (multiple CEO changes = dysfunction). Determine which applies here.

tasks.prompt: BLACKSTONE OWNS 22.93% OF BMBL (29.9M shares) as of Mar 31, 2026. This is HIGHER than previously reported estimates of 14-15%. Questions: 1) Has Blackstone been BUYING more shares or has their percentage increased due to buybacks reducing float? 2) At 22.93%, Blackstone is the single largest holder. Does this give them effective control? 3) Blackstone has $1T+ AUM — their $96M BMBL position is trivial. Why are they holding? 4) Could Blackstone orchestrate a take-private at these levels? 5) What is Blackstone's track record with distressed portfolio companies?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a private equity analyst. A 22.93% stake is a controlling position. Determine Blackstone's likely strategy — hold, sell, or take private.

tasks.prompt: BMBL Q1 2026 EARNINGS BEAT: Revenue $212.4M (vs estimate $211.6M, slight beat). EPS $0.35 (vs estimate $0.27, 26% BEAT). Net income $45.2M (up 236% from Q1 2025 $13.4M). Profit margin 21% (up from 5.4%). Adjusted EBITDA $83M (+29.7% YoY). Gross margin expanded 300bps YoY. Questions: 1) How is EPS $0.35 when revenue declined 14%? Pure cost cutting? 2) Is the margin expansion sustainable or one-time? 3) BofA raised price target after this beat — to what? 4) Stock DROPPED 19% after the beat (from $4.25 to $3.43). Why sell after a beat?
tasks.system_prompt: You are an earnings analysis expert. A stock dropping 19% after beating estimates means the market doesn't believe the beat is sustainable. Investigate why.

tasks.prompt: BMBL Q2 2026 GUIDANCE: Revenue $205M-$213M. Q1 2026 actual was $212.4M. Q2 2025 was $248.2M. So Q2 2026 guidance implies -14% to -17% YoY decline, and potentially FLAT to SLIGHTLY DECLINING QoQ. Questions: 1) Is -14% to -17% YoY better or worse than Q1's -14.2%? 2) Midpoint $209M vs Q1 $212.4M = -1.4% QoQ — is the SEQUENTIAL decline slowing? 3) If Q2 prints $209M and Q3 guidance is similar, does that mean revenue stabilizes around $205-210M/quarter (~$830M annualized)? 4) Management also mentioned Bumble App Revenue guidance $171-174M — what is the Badoo implied revenue?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a revenue forecasting analyst. The Q2 guidance is CRITICAL — it tells us if the revenue decline is decelerating. Analyze the implied trajectory.

tasks.prompt: BMBL AI PLATFORM LAUNCH: In Q1 2026 earnings call, CEO Whitney Wolfe Herd announced rollout of a new 'cloud-native, AI-enabled platform starting in coming weeks, with global expansion planned.' Questions: 1) What is this AI platform? AI matching? AI conversation starters? AI profile writing? 2) Is this a genuine product innovation or marketing buzzword? 3) How does this compare to Tinder's AI features? Hinge's AI? 4) Could an AI-powered dating experience actually improve retention and reduce churn? 5) What is the timeline for global rollout?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a product strategy analyst specializing in AI consumer applications. Assess whether Bumble's AI platform is a real differentiator or vapor.

tasks.prompt: BMBL ANALYST RATINGS: 0 Buy, 15 Hold, 1 Sell (BofA at Sell, $3.50 target). Average target $4.34 (+42.8% upside). UBS Hold $4.50. Deutsche Bank Hold $4.00. BofA Sell $3.50. Questions: 1) Why zero Buy ratings? Is the consensus too bearish? 2) Average target $4.34 is 42.8% above current — why not Buy if they see 43% upside? 3) BofA is the lone Sell — what is their thesis? 4) SimplyWallSt fair value $9 (66% undervalued) — massive disconnect from analyst targets. Who is right? 5) Has any analyst upgraded recently?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a sell-side research analyst. Zero Buys with 43% upside is unusual. Determine if analysts are wrong (contrarian opportunity) or if the risks justify Hold.

tasks.prompt: BMBL MARGIN EXPANSION STORY: Q1 2026: Gross margin expanded 300bps YoY. Adjusted EBITDA $83M (+29.7%). Operating margin 31.5%. Only 580 employees. Revenue/employee $1.6M. Management is clearly cutting costs aggressively. Questions: 1) What costs have been cut? Marketing spend? Engineering? Content moderation? 2) Is the company now in 'harvest mode' — maximizing profit from declining revenue? 3) Can margins expand further even as revenue declines? 4) Is there a risk of cutting too deep — underinvesting in product leads to faster user decline? 5) What is the optimal margin vs growth tradeoff?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a SaaS operations analyst. Companies can temporarily boost margins by cutting costs, but this accelerates revenue decline if underinvesting. Assess Bumble's balance.

tasks.prompt: DEEPSEEK ERROR AUDIT: Sprint 13 (40 agents analyzing BMBL) produced 3 VERIFIED ERRORS vs real data from Investing.com and SimplyWallSt: 1) DeepSeek said CEO is Lidiane Jones — WRONG, Whitney Wolfe Herd returned as CEO Mar 2025. 2) DeepSeek said Blackstone owns 14-15% — WRONG, actually 22.93%. 3) DeepSeek said $0 buybacks — WRONG, buyback yield is 1.5%. Why did DeepSeek get these wrong? Likely reasons: training data cutoff, hallucination, or outdated SEC filings. What other DeepSeek claims from Sprint 13 should we now treat as unverified?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a data quality analyst. Three verified errors in 40 tasks = 7.5% error rate on factual claims. Assess which other Sprint 13 claims need SEC filing verification.

tasks.prompt: BMBL FAIR VALUE ANALYSIS: SimplyWallSt calculates fair value at $9.00 (66.2% undervalued). Community fair values range $8.65-$9.20. Investing.com analyst average target $4.34. Questions: 1) SimplyWallSt uses DCF model — what discount rate and growth assumptions produce $9? 2) Is $9 realistic given revenue is declining -14%? 3) The community/analyst gap ($9 vs $4.34) is massive — who is right? 4) SimplyWallSt gives 6/6 on valuation score — what criteria? 5) Forward ROE 17.1% in 3 years — is this achievable with declining revenue?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a valuation model analyst. Determine whether the $9 DCF fair value is realistic or overly optimistic given the revenue decline trajectory.

tasks.prompt: BMBL TECHNICAL ANALYSIS: Current $3.04. RSI(14d) 32.14 (near oversold). 50-day $3.61, 200-day $4.26. All timeframes showing 'Strong Sell' on technicals. Beta 2.00. 1-month -26.92%. 3-month +2.70%. 1-year -43.39%. Volume 2.8M vs avg 4.1M (below average). 52w range $2.61-$8.64. Questions: 1) RSI 32 — is this an oversold bounce setup? Historical bounces at RSI <30? 2) What support levels exist below $3.04? $2.61 (52w low), $2.00? 3) Is there a technical pattern forming (falling wedge, descending channel)? 4) Volume below average — capitulation not yet complete? 5) Where would a technical buy signal trigger?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a technical analysis expert. The chart shows a sustained downtrend. Identify if there are any bullish reversal signals or if more downside is likely.

tasks.prompt: BMBL EARNINGS GROWTH TRAJECTORY: Analysts forecast EPS growth 108.77% p.a. (losses shrinking rapidly). Q1'25 EPS $0.13, Q1'26 EPS $0.35 (+169%). Forward P/E 3.03x. Revenue declining but EPS growing = margin expansion story. Questions: 1) If EPS grows from $0.35/quarter to $0.50/quarter, annualized EPS = $2.00. At 10x P/E = $20. At 5x P/E = $10. Is this realistic? 2) What is the sustainable EPS power assuming revenue stabilizes at $830M? 3) Can EPS growth offset revenue decline for 3+ years? 4) At what revenue level does EPS growth stall (can't cut more)?
tasks.system_prompt: You are an earnings power analyst. Model the EPS trajectory assuming continued cost cuts but declining revenue. Find the equilibrium point.

tasks.prompt: WHITNEY WOLFE HERD INSIDER SELLING: In Aug 2025, Whitney exercised options to acquire 1M shares at no cost and sold them for $6.3M at $6.26/share. This was the ONLY insider transaction in 12 months. Questions: 1) She exercised free options and sold — is this normal executive compensation (take the free stock, sell for income) or a red flag? 2) She sold at $6.26 — stock is now $3.04. She timed the top well. Did she know something? 3) Her direct holding increased from 654.5K to 1.43M shares — so she kept some. 4) At 0.5% ownership, she has minimal skin in the game. Is that concerning for a founder-CEO?
tasks.system_prompt: You are an insider trading pattern analyst. Distinguish between routine compensation sales and conviction selling. A founder selling at $6.26 who then watches stock fall to $3.04 — what does this tell us?

tasks.prompt: BMBL NEW CFO: Kevin D. Cook appointed August 2025. Background: ex-Cloudera CFO (2021-2023), ex-Cloudera SVP Finance (2014-2021), ex-Barracuda Networks VP, ex-investment banker (Cowen, Credit Suisse, Wachovia, RBC). UCLA Economics-Business BA, Georgetown JD. Age 61. Questions: 1) Is this a strong hire? Cloudera was acquired by PE in 2021 and later went public again — relevant experience? 2) Investment banking background + PE experience = good for M&A? 3) Why did previous CFO (Ronald Fior) leave? 4) New CPO Michael Affronti also from Salesforce. Is there a Salesforce pipeline at Bumble?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a CFO assessment analyst. Evaluate whether Kevin Cook is a turnaround CFO, an M&A-oriented CFO, or a harvest-mode CFO.

tasks.prompt: BMBL MANAGEMENT TURNOVER: Average management tenure is only 1.2 YEARS. Board average tenure is 5.8 years. Multiple C-suite changes: CEO changed twice (Whitney → Jones → Whitney), CFO changed (Fior → Cook), CPO changed (Rayl → Affronti). Questions: 1) Is 1.2-year average tenure a red flag? Companies in turnaround often have high turnover, but stability is needed to execute. 2) Does Whitney's return provide stability or is she a placeholder? 3) Annual General Meeting is Jun 04, 2026 — any expected board changes? 4) Total CEO comp $7.62M (8.5% salary, 91.5% stock) — is this aligned with shareholders?
tasks.system_prompt: You are an organizational behavior analyst. High executive turnover destroys strategy execution. Assess whether BMBL's leadership is stabilizing or still in flux.

tasks.prompt: BMBL NEW PRODUCT: 'Bumble to launch paid group dating feature amid revenue decline.' This is a NEW product announced ~Jun 2026. Questions: 1) What is group dating? Is it like double dates, group activities, social events? 2) Is this a genuine product innovation or a desperate pivot? 3) Could group dating expand TAM beyond traditional 1:1 dating? 4) Revenue potential — would users pay extra for group features? 5) Competitors doing anything similar? 6) Is this Whitney's vision for reviving Bumble?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a consumer product strategist. Assess whether group dating is a meaningful product innovation or a gimmick to slow revenue decline.

tasks.prompt: BMBL REVENUE FLOOR ANALYSIS: Revenue trajectory: 2024 $1,071.6M → 2025 $965.7M (-9.9%) → Q1'26 annualized ~$850M. Analysts forecast -4.9% p.a. average decline. Q2 guidance $205-213M (midpoint $209M). Questions: 1) At -4.9% p.a. decline, revenue in 2029 = $850M * (0.951)^3 = ~$726M. Is this realistic? 2) What is the revenue FLOOR — at what level does Bumble's user base stabilize? 3) Badoo is dying — what is Bumble App-only revenue? If Bumble App is $171-174M/quarter = $688M annualized, is THAT the real floor? 4) Could Badoo be divested or shut down to stop the bleed?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a revenue floor analyst. Every declining business has a natural floor where the core user base stabilizes. Find Bumble's.

tasks.prompt: BMBL EBITDA VALUATION: EBITDA $284.9M. EV $866.3M. EV/EBITDA 3.04x. This is EXTREMELY cheap for a tech company. Questions: 1) What do comparable dating/social companies trade at on EV/EBITDA? MTCH? GRND? 2) If BMBL traded at 6x EV/EBITDA (still cheap), EV = $1,710M. Minus debt + cash = equity $1,358M / 130.4M shares = $10.42/share. 3) At 8x EV/EBITDA, stock = $14.81/share. 4) Is 3x EV/EBITDA pricing in bankruptcy risk? 5) PE firms typically buy at 8-12x EV/EBITDA for stable cash flows. Even at discount (6x), that's $10+ per share. Why is nobody bidding?
tasks.system_prompt: You are an EV/EBITDA valuation analyst. 3x EV/EBITDA for a profitable tech company is almost unheard of. Calculate what the stock should trade at using peer multiples.

tasks.prompt: BMBL PRICE ACTION FORENSIC: Stock DROPPED 19% (from $4.25 to $3.43) after BEATING Q1 estimates on May 5, 2026. Then continued falling to $3.04. Questions: 1) Why does a stock drop after a beat? Usually means: a) guidance was weak, b) quality of beat was low, c) short-term holders exiting. 2) Q2 guidance was $205-213M — was this below expectations? 3) Is this a classic 'sell the news' pattern? 4) The stock went from $8.64 high to $3.04 in one year (-65%). Is this capitulation or is there more downside? 5) What happened to similar stocks after post-beat selloffs?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a price action analyst. A -19% move after a beat is extremely bearish. Determine if this is final capitulation or a structural downtrend continuing.

Calculate probability-weighted EV.

tasks.prompt: BMBL KILL TEST: Apply our kill criteria ruthlessly. Kill if: 1) Chronic dilution >10%/yr — BMBL shares outstanding 130.4M. Has this been increasing?
